properties.name: The per-client reply shape already implements all three options flo2 asks for, and its DEFAULT is the one shape that serves neither population — which is what every new connector gets, by construction
properties.statement:
FLO2 F26 argues that the text block carrying a placeholder sentence is 'wrong for every reader': an old client gets one useless sentence instead of the payload, and a TEXT-FIRST client that reads structuredContent only when the text is empty is defeated by the non-empty placeholder. They name three shapes — (a) placeholder, (b) empty, (c) the serialized payload — and ask for (c) on the tools a remote consumer reaches.

⭐ MEASURED 2026-09-20, AND ALL THREE ALREADY EXIST. content_policy.rs serves exactly (a) Signpost, (b) Empty and (c) Duplicate, chosen per client at handshake by name: a client whose name starts with `grok` gets the payload in the text block, a name containing `opencode` gets an empty one, and EVERY OTHER CLIENT GETS THE SIGNPOST. There is also a `--content-policy` override. So the mechanism flo2 asks for is built, and was built from two measured clients (fact:grok-build-measured-on-this-box…, and the OpenCode measurement).

🛑 SO THE DEFECT IS NARROWER AND SHARPER THAN REPORTED, AND IT IS IN THE DEFAULT. The fallback is Signpost — the one shape flo2 shows fails both populations — and a client is matched BY NAME, so anything not called grok or opencode gets it. Every connector flo2 is about to point at this server is unknown by construction: Claude, ChatGPT and Grok connectors have never been measured here, and a name-keyed policy cannot learn.

⚠️ AND THE SIGNPOST WAS CHOSEN DELIBERATELY, WITH A REASON FLO2 DOES NOT HAVE. fact:every-reply-was-sent-twice records it: an empty content block saves the same bytes, and the signpost costs ~450 bytes 'and is what a client reading the wrong field gets INSTEAD OF SILENCE. Silence there is indistinguishable from reflow2 never having been configured', which is req:never-silently-absent. That reasoning is sound and it did not account for a client that treats a non-empty text block as the answer. THE TWO GOALS ARE CONTRADICTORY, and flo2 states it exactly: you cannot keep the text non-empty AND have an empty-fallback client read the structured object.

⚠️ VERSION-GATING IS ALREADY REFUTED, twice over: fact:every-reply-was-sent-twice killed it by measurement, and flo2 independently reaches the same conclusion — population 1 (pre-2025-06-18) is visible on every request and population 2 is INVISIBLE, since no client capability says 'I read structuredContent'. Gating on the negotiated version would not have fixed the only failure anyone has observed.
